outcome.support: עשויים להיווצר מצבים שבהם חוק חורג - התקף לעניין חוק-יסוד: חופש העיסוק - יימצא כבלתי תקף לעניין חוק-יסוד: כבוד האדם וחירותו (para 18, p. 29)
outcome.note: Second reading, 22 October 2026, replacing the first docket reader's Not adverse (recorded below). Nine justices, unanimous, Barak P. writing the sole reasoned opinion; petition dismissed and the order nisi cancelled; the Meat and Meat Products Law 1994, enacted under the override clause, upheld. Coded Adverse under step 4's rule that upheld-and-narrowed is Adverse: the ratio of paras 18 and 21–23 holds that an override law is protected only within Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation, may be found invalid under Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty, and is shielded there only on three cumulative conditions (the dignity infringement a natural side-effect of the occupational one, the occupational infringement the principal one, the other not of real force), applied to the facts in para 23 and the basis of dismissal in para 24. Para 15 (the clause cannot validate a law that abolishes the right altogether) is a general statement not applied; para 16 (basic principles an override law cannot infringe) is expressly left undecided. Alternative reading, Not adverse: section 8's own words shield an override law only against section 4 of the same Basic Law, so holding that it does not immunise a law under the other Basic Law is a literal application, and the three-condition test extends the clause's effect to incidental dignity infringements rather than narrowing it; the Court reasoned on three assumptions arguendo and declined to decide them. Confidence medium: the facts are from the full report; the coding turns on whether confining the clause to its own Basic Law and extending it conditionally counts as narrowing. The text read is an OCR layer with minor artefacts; a reader with Nevo access should confirm against the live file.
